content: The text provided appears to be a list of references, primarily from medical and public health literature, detailing various studies, guidelines, and systematic reviews. 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) published the AWaRe Antibiotic Book in 2022, which categorizes antibiotics into Access, Watch, and Reserve groups to guide their appropriate use and combat antimicrobial resistance. This resource is available online via the WHO IRIS platform. 2. WHO released guidelines in 2016 for the treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections, emphasizing evidence-based approaches to address antimicrobial resistance. These guidelines are accessible through the WHO IRIS repository. 3. In 2016, WHO also published treatment guidelines for Chlamydia trachomatis infections, providing recommendations for effective management in various clinical settings. 4. WHO developed specific guidelines for the treatment of Treponema pallidum (syphilis), focusing on evidence-based therapeutic strategies to improve patient outcomes. 5. WHO issued comprehensive guidelines on hepatitis B and C testing, aiming to enhance early diagnosis and linkage to care. These guidelines are available on the WHO IRIS platform. 6. Interim guidance on surveillance, case investigation, and contact tracing for mpox (monkeypox) was released by WHO on December 22, 2022, to support public health responses to outbreaks. 7. WHO and the International Labour Organization (ILO) jointly published policy guidelines to improve health worker access to prevention, treatment, and care services for HIV and tuberculosis (TB). 8. WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis screening (Module 2) provide systematic approaches for identifying TB cases, emphasizing early detection and intervention. 9. The Global Outbreak Alert and Response Network (GOARN) serves as a collaborative platform to enhance global preparedness and response to infectious disease outbreaks. 10. The WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd edition, 2014) outlines standardized methods for creating evidence-based health guidelines. 11. The GRADEpro Guideline Development Tool (GDT) is a software resource designed to facilitate the development of clinical and public health guidelines. 12. The Enhanced Gonococcal Antimicrobial Surveillance Programme (EGASP) provides a general protocol for monitoring antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae. 13. A 2022 study by Cole et al. in Euro Surveillance highlights the European response to controlling multiand extensively drug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae. 14. Paez-Canro et al. conducted a Cochrane systematic review on antibiotics for treating urogenital Chlamydia trachomatis infections in men and non-pregnant women. 15. Machalek et al. performed a systematic review and meta-analysis on mutations associated with resistance to macrolides and fluoroquinolones in Mycoplasma genitalium, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 16. Updated WHO recommendations address the treatment of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, and syphilis, alongside new guidance on syphilis testing and partner services. 17. Read et al. evaluated outcomes of resistance-guided sequential treatment for Mycoplasma genitalium infections in a prospective study published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 18. Ryan et al. reviewed interventions to improve the safe and effective use of medicines by consumers, summarizing findings from systematic reviews in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 19. Mabilat et al. reviewed current practices and unmet needs in improving antimicrobial stewardship through penicillin allergy testing, published in JAC Antimicrobial Resistance. 20. The UNICEF Supply Catalogue provides essential medical supplies and resources for global health programs. 21. WHO, UNFPA, UNAIDS, the World Bank, and other organizations collaborated on a guide for implementing comprehensive HIV/STI programs with sex workers, emphasizing practical approaches for collaborative interventions. 22. A similar guide was developed for HIV/STI programs targeting men who have sex with men (MSM), published by UNFPA and other partners. 23. Another guide focuses on implementing HIV/STI programs with transgender populations, developed by WHO, UNDP, and other organizations. 24. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and partners published guidance on comprehensive HIV and HCV programs for people who inject drugs, emphasizing harm reduction strategies. 25. Wu et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the impact of syphilis infection on HIV acquisition, published in Sexually Transmitted Infections. 26. Sena et al. identified predictors of serological cure and serofast states after syphilis treatment in HIV-negative individuals, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 27. Zhang et al. explored molecular subtyping of Treponema pallidum and associated factors of serofast status in early syphilis patients, identifying novel genotypes and cytokine markers. 28. WHO published a manual on laboratory and point-of-care diagnostic testing for sexually transmitted infections, including HIV. 29. The Joint United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) launched the Laws and Policies Analytics website to track legal and policy frameworks affecting HIV responses. 30. The Global Sexually Transmitted Infections Programme provides strategic information and resources to support STI prevention and control efforts. 31. Abdulai et al. reported on increasing syphilis testing coverage in antenatal care in Ghana through the rollout of dual HIV/syphilis rapid diagnostic tests. 32. WHO published guidance on syphilis testing in Latin America and the Caribbean, focusing on improving test uptake, interpretation, and quality in clinical settings. 33. WHO recommendations for HIV and STI prevention and treatment among MSM and transgender populations emphasize a public health approach. 34. Zhang et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on improved rapid diagnostic tests for syphilis and yaws, published in Sexually Transmitted Infections. 35. WHO developed a guide for yaws eradication program managers, focusing on surveillance, monitoring, and evaluation. 36. Terris-Prestholt et al. assessed the cost-effectiveness of antenatal syphilis screening and treatment approaches in Peru, Tanzania, and Zambia. 37. WHO issued recommendations on hepatitis C virus self-testing to enhance diagnosis and linkage to care. 38. WHO's 2022 revision of the guideline on self-care interventions for health and well-being provides updated recommendations for empowering individuals in managing their health. 39. WHO released interim guidance on the use of SARS-CoV-2 antigen-detection rapid diagnostic tests for COVID-19 self-testing. 40. Towns et al. reviewed the role of syphilis self-testing as an additional testing approach for key populations, published in The Lancet Public Health. 41. Balán et al. developed the SMARTtest smartphone app to facilitate HIV and syphilis selfand partner-testing, result interpretation, and linkage to care. 42. Lentz et al. explored the negotiation of dual HIV/syphilis test use with potential sexual partners among cisgender men and transgender women in New York City. 43. Nhamo et al. evaluated the feasibility and economic costs of syphilis self-testing to expand test uptake among gay, bisexual, and transgender men in Zimbabwe. 44. Wang et al. conducted a nationwide pragmatic study on syphilis self-testing among MSM in China, published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 45. WHO's updated recommendations for treating Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, and syphilis include new guidance on syphilis testing and partner services. 46. Sri-Pathmanathan et al. conducted a mixed-methods study on syphilis self-testing to expand test uptake among MSM in Zimbabwe. 47. Wang et al. examined syphilis self-testing among female sex workers in China, highlighting implications for expanding syphilis screening. 48. Wu et al. investigated social media-based secondary distribution of HIV/syphilis self-testing among Chinese MSM. 49. Yang et al. analyzed the distribution of HIV/syphilis self-tests by sexual health influencers among MSM in China to inform community-based interventions. 50. Zhong et al. assessed the acceptability and feasibility of a social entrepreneurship testing model to promote HIV self-testing among MSM. 51. Figueroa et al. reviewed the reliability of HIV rapid diagnostic tests for self-testing compared to testing by healthcare workers. 52. Reipold et al. presented multicountry evidence on the usability and acceptability of HCV self-testing. 53. Rael et al. explored transgender women's experiences using home HIV-testing kits for partner testing. 54. Eshun-Wilson et al. conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of HIV self-testing distribution strategies. 55. Nichols et al. performed an economic evaluation of facility-based HIV self-testing among adult outpatients in Malawi. 56. Galvão et al. reviewed the safety of benzathine penicillin for preventing congenital syphilis. 57. Simo Fotso et al. analyzed routine programmatic data showing the population-level impact of HIV self-testing in Côte d’Ivoire. 58. Rothschild et al. developed a measurement tool for sexual and reproductive health self-care. 59. Dalal et al. reviewed the impact of assisted partner notification services on improving HIV test uptake and case finding. 60. Begun et al. conducted a systematic review of transmission modeling studies on tuberculosis contact tracing. 61. Juneau et al. reviewed the effectiveness of contact tracing for COVID-19. 62. Saurabh et al. examined the role of contact tracing in containing the 2014 Ebola outbreak. 63. Katzman et al. discussed novel screening strategies for hepatitis C contact tracing to achieve viral elimination.
